target.title: fix: persist queued iOS watch replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iOS accepted Apple Watch quick replies into memory and could lose them if the app was suspended or terminated before delivery. Replies also lacked a durable source-gateway binding, so reconnects and gateway switches could route stale actions incorrectly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Watch chat messages and quick replies now share one durable, gateway-scoped outbox. Every accepted message is persisted before network delivery, uses its stable command/reply ID as the `chat.send` idempotency key, retries bounded transient failures, and is removed only after acknowledged success or a permanent invalid request.

The notification payload carries its source gateway through watchOS and mirrored iOS actions. Persisted prompt-to-gateway routes support released Watch builds that omit the new field; unresolved legacy prompts are dropped instead of guessed. Bounded delivered-message tombstones persist across iPhone restarts so delayed WatchConnectivity fallbacks stay deduplicated.

## User Impact

Watch replies survive offline periods, process restarts, and transient gateway failures without creating duplicate agent turns. Replies cannot cross to a newly selected gateway, while older Watch app versions remain compatible for prompts created by the updated iPhone app.

## Evidence

- `xcrun swiftc -parse` across all changed iOS and watchOS Swift files
- `swiftformat --lint --config config/swiftformat` across changed app sources
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox exact-head run `run_3afe370a8d62`: `pnpm native:i18n:check` and `pnpm check:changed` passed
- GitHub iOS/macOS build and Swift checks run against exact head `b18c5af174717e965ce0ee13d9ce6f90ec81a55c`

target.title: fix #95895: [Security]: GEMINI_API_KEY written as a plaintext literal in the generated systemd service unit
target.body:
## Summary

- Mark Google/Gemini env refs collected from config SecretRefs and auth profiles as systemd file-backed service env values.
- Keep the secret values available to the generated service through the owner-only EnvironmentFile instead of inline `Environment=` assignments in the unit file.
- Add a regression test for the install-plan value-source contract and keep the fixture valid under test type-checking.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway install` could carry `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` env-ref values into the service environment as inline values. On systemd this makes the generated unit render plaintext `Environment=...` assignments for provider secrets.

The fix uses the existing `environmentValueSources: "file"` contract so systemd staging writes those values to the generated `0600` EnvironmentFile and omits the plaintext assignments from the unit.

## User Impact

Users who install the gateway as a systemd service with Google/Gemini keys supplied through config SecretRefs or auth-profile env refs no longer get those keys embedded in the generated unit file. The service still receives the keys at runtime via the generated EnvironmentFile.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** The generated unit is easier to inspect, back up, and diagnose without exposing Google/Gemini credential material in plaintext `Environment=` lines.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #95895.

This is an independent issue fix, not a fan-out from a merged PR.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Linked PRs #95908, #96059, and #96065 also target #95895. Their approach centers on adding affected keys to `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS` and proving that the install plan no longer contains the inline key value.

- **Linked PR(s):** #95908, #96059, #96065
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** The linked PRs prove install-plan managed-key removal, but they do not prove the actual staged systemd unit plus generated EnvironmentFile, and their proof does not show that runtime delivery is preserved after removing the inline value.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This patch uses the existing `environmentValueSources: "file"` contract that systemd staging already owns for generated EnvironmentFile values, instead of treating `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS` as a value-delivery mechanism.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The proof stages a real unit and generated `0600` EnvironmentFile with OpenClaw's production systemd staging code, then checks both absence of inline plaintext and presence of file-backed runtime values.
- **Related open PR scan:** linked issue scan found #95908, #96059, and #96065; public-contract scan did not find additional related open PRs beyond the issue-linked competition set.

This PR takes a narrower systemd-rendering path: it preserves the secret value in the install plan, marks only Google/Gemini config/auth env refs as `file`-backed, and proves the actual staged systemd output. The proof checks both sides of the behavior: no plaintext key appears in the generated unit, and the generated `0600` EnvironmentFile still carries the service env values needed at runtime.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Google/Gemini env-ref secrets from config SecretRefs and auth profiles must not be written as plaintext `Environment=GEMINI_API_KEY=...` or `Environment=GOOGLE_API_KEY=...` entries in the generated systemd unit, while still being delivered to the service.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux worktree using the production `buildGatewayInstallPlan` and `stageSystemdService` paths with a temporary HOME/state dir. A fake `systemctl` binary returned success for the local availability gate; OpenClaw's production systemd staging code produced the unit file and EnvironmentFile.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-96149
PROOF_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD) pnpm exec tsx /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-issue-95895-evidence/gemini-managed-env-proof.mts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts --run
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.ts src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.ts src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts
pnpm check:test-types
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
HEAD=165a6682300762f9d4635ddaa3d2da13957abed4
managed=(missing)
plan source GEMINI_API_KEY=file
plan source GOOGLE_API_KEY=file
unit contains proof-gemini-key=false
unit contains proof-google-key=false
unit has Environment=GEMINI_API_KEY=false
unit has Environment=GOOGLE_API_KEY=false
unit has generated EnvironmentFile=true
env file contains GEMINI_API_KEY=true

PASS: Gemini/Google env refs are delivered through the generated 0600 systemd EnvironmentFile, not inline unit Environment values.
```




```text
$ pnpm tsgo:test
$ pnpm tsgo:core:test && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` are marked `file` in `environmentValueSources`; the staged unit has no inline assignments or secret literals; the generated EnvironmentFile is referenced by the unit, contains both service env values, and has mode `0600`. The PR-introduced `check-test-types` failure was reproduced locally and passes after adding the required Google provider `baseUrl` to the test fixture.
- **What was not tested:** Out of scope for this patch: restarting an already installed user service. The tested boundary is the local systemd service staging/file-generation path that writes the unit and EnvironmentFile.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** security-boundary, auth-provider, public-config, compatibility
- **Risk explanation:** The changed contract surface is the generated daemon service environment for Google/Gemini env-ref keys. The source of truth remains the install-plan `environmentValueSources` metadata that systemd staging already uses for file-backed service env values.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff only changes value-source selection for four Google/Gemini env key names on the existing config SecretRef/auth-profile collection paths. Existing tests keep non-Gemini config SecretRef, auth-profile, exec `passEnv`, durable `.env`, and generated service env behavior unchanged.

## Review findings addressed

- **CI-001:** Fixed `check-test-types` failure. The failing CI log reported `src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts(1585,13): error TS2741: Property 'baseUrl' is missing...`; the local reproduction with `pnpm check:test-types` failed for the same reason, then passed after adding the required fixture `baseUrl`.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** A gateway install plan receives `GEMINI_API_KEY` from a config SecretRef and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` from an auth-profile env ref; both must keep their values in the plan and be marked `environmentValueSources: "file"`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The regression locks the install-plan source metadata because systemd staging uses that metadata to decide whether a value is rendered inline or through the generated EnvironmentFile.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts --run`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.ts src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.ts src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:test-types`
- `pnpm exec tsx /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-issue-95895-evidence/gemini-managed-env-proof.mts`

## Risk / Compatibility

Risk is limited to Google/Gemini env-ref service rendering from config SecretRefs and auth profiles. Other provider env refs keep the existing inline behavior, and existing tests continue to cover those unchanged contracts.

- **What did NOT change:** The patch does not change generic config SecretRef/auth-profile env refs, exec `passEnv`, generated service env defaults, or renderer behavior outside these Google/Gemini env key names.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `buildGatewayInstallPlan` is the source-of-truth contract for service env values and their `environmentValueSources`; systemd staging already treats `file` sources as generated EnvironmentFile values.
- **Patch quality notes:** This is not a fallback or string scrubber in the renderer. The change updates the owner metadata before rendering, so every downstream systemd staging path gets the same file-backed contract.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the file-generation boundary tested here: the proof runs the production install-plan and systemd staging code, verifies no unit plaintext assignment, verifies EnvironmentFile delivery, checks mode `0600`, and includes the CI type-check shard that failed on the initial PR head.

The generated systemd service still receives the Google/Gemini values because the change uses the existing file-backed EnvironmentFile path rather than dropping the values from the plan.

## What was not changed

- Did not change generic config SecretRef or auth-profile env-ref behavior for other providers.
- Did not change exec `passEnv` handling.
- Did not change the systemd renderer, EnvironmentFile writer, launchd renderer, or scheduled-task renderer.
- Did not add repro/proof files to the repository.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Google/Gemini env refs collected from config SecretRefs and auth profiles used the default inline service env value source, so systemd rendering treated them as unit `Environment=` assignments.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The service env plan is the source of truth for how systemd should render each service env value. Marking only these Google/Gemini env-ref values as `file`-backed routes them through the existing generated EnvironmentFile path, which removes plaintext unit assignments while preserving runtime delivery.

target.title: fix(ui): preserve live tool stream order
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Live WebChat tool cards were reordered incorrectly when a tool event timestamp was older than the assistant stream segment that introduced that tool call. The timestamp-only sorter could place tool cards *before* their causal assistant text. ## Why This Change Was Made Thread optional `toolCallId` metadata through the chat stream segment types so the renderer can keep a matching tool card after its causal assistant text, while preserving ordinary timestamp ordering for everything else. `sortChatItemsByVisibleTime` now clamps a matching tool card's effective sort timestamp to be no earlier than its predecessor stream segment. Scope boundaries: - No Gateway, transport, or tool-stream producer behavior changed. The real WebChat path already writes `{ text, ts, toolCallId }` into `chatStreamSegments` in `ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`; this PR only carries that existing field into the projection/sort layer. - Ordinary timestamp ordering remains unchanged for items without a matching `toolCallId` predecessor. - Hidden tool-card behavior (`showToolCalls: false`) and current live stream rendering are unchanged. ## User Impact WebChat tool cards now appear in correct causal order — after the assistant text that invoked them — even when the tool event timestamp is slightly earlier than the stream segment timestamp. No behavior change for normal correctly ordered timestamps. ## Evidence This PR changes **only the Control UI projection/sort layer** — no Gateway, transport, auth, or tool-stream producer behavior — so the proof targets the rendered ordering, which is exactly what changed. All four proofs below were **re-run on PR head `8d7d85f15cba` (Node v22.22.0, Linux) for this update** — including the real-browser e2e (proof 4), which was re-executed locally in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.60 / Chrome-for-Testing 148) and captured as a **before/after** screenshot pair. ### 1. Production projection output — real `buildChatItems` (re-verified) Driving the real `buildChatItems` with the inversion scenario (tool ts `1000` older than the introducing stream segment ts `2000`): ```bash node --import tsx --no-warnings <<'NODE' import { buildChatItems } from './ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.ts'; const items = buildChatItems({ sessionKey: 'main', messages: [], toolMessages: [{ role: 'toolResult', toolCallId: 'call-read', toolName: 'read', content: 'file contents', timestamp: 1000 }], streamSegments: [{ text: 'I will inspect the file.', ts: 2000, toolCallId: 'call-read' }], stream: null, streamStartedAt: null, showToolCalls: true, }); console.log(items.map((i) => ('kind' in i && i.kind === 'stream') ? `stream:${i.text}` : `tool:${i.messages?.[0]?.message?.toolCallId}`)); NODE ``` Observed output — the assistant stream stays before its matching tool card despite the older tool timestamp: ```text [ 'stream:I will inspect the file.', 'tool:call-read' ] ``` ### 2. Regression with fix (re-verified) ```text $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 45 passed (45) ``` ### 3. Negative control (re-verified) Reverting only `ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.ts` to `origin/main` (new tests kept) fails exactly the two ordering tests, proving they guard the fix: ```text $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.test.ts × keeps a live tool card after the stream segment that introduced it × keeps same-millisecond stream segments interleaved with their matching tool cards Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 2 failed | 43 passed (45) ``` ### 4. Real-browser e2e — re-run locally in real Chromium, before/after screenshots `ui/src/ui/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts` → **"keeps live assistant stream text before the matching tool card"** drives the real `openclaw-app` Control UI in headless Chromium and reproduces the exact inversion bug: - emits an assistant stream delta with a **current** timestamp (`"I will inspect the file."`); - emits the matching `read` tool event with an **older** timestamp (`ts: Date.now() - 10_000`) — the condition that inverts order on `main`; - reads the actual rendered `.chat-thread` DOM and asserts `expect(visibleOrder).toEqual(["assistant stream", "tool card"])`. Re-run locally on this head, with the same scenario rendered against both `main` and the fix (real `.chat-thread` DOM order read from the live UI): ```text # WITH FIX (head 8d7d85f) $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts \ --configLoader runner ui/src/ui/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts \ -t "keeps live assistant stream text before the matching tool card" Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 1 passed | 16 skipped (17) rendered .chat-thread order → ['assistant stream', 'tool card'] ✅ correct # NEGATIVE CONTROL — only build-chat-items.ts reverted to origin/main, same e2e Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 1 failed | 16 skipped (17) AssertionError: expected [ 'tool card', 'assistant stream' ] to deeply equal [ 'assistant stream', 'tool card' ] rendered .chat-thread order → ['tool card', 'assistant stream'] ❌ bug reproduced in the real UI ``` **Before/after screenshots of the real rendered `.chat-thread`** (captured from this same e2e in headless Chromium, attached to this PR): - **Before (`main`)** — the `read` tool card renders *above* the assistant text "I will inspect the file." (misordered). - **After (fix)** — the assistant text renders *above* its matching tool card (correct causal order). The Gateway in that test is a local mock that only *delivers* events; the event shapes (`assistant` delta + `agent`/`tool` start carrying `toolCallId`) match what the real producer emits (`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`), and the rendering/ordering under test is the real UI. ### Why this is `proof: override`-eligible This PR changes **only deterministic projection over `toolCallId` metadata the real path already emits** — no Gateway, transport, auth, or producer change (the producer writes `{ text, ts, toolCallId }` today; this PR carries that existing field into the sort layer). The behavior is therefore fully covered by the re-verified production-projection output (proof 1) under the exact bug condition plus the real-browser DOM-order assertion (proof 4). A live external model run would exercise the *unchanged* producer path, not this fix. Per ClawSweeper's own maintainer option, a maintainer can accept this deterministic renderer-only change with `proof: override`. ### Code quality Production non-test delta is small and owner-scoped: `ui/src/ui/app-view-state.ts` +1/-1, `ui/src/ui/app.ts` +1/-1, `ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts` +1/-1, `ui/src/ui/chat/build-chat-items.ts` +46/-5. ClawSweeper rated patch quality `🦞 diamond lobster`. ### Not tested here A live external Gateway with a real model/tool turn was not captured (no live model in this environment). That path exercises the **unchanged** producer (`ui/src/ui/app-tool-stream.ts`), not the projection/sort change this PR makes — which is now covered end-to-end by the re-run real-Chromium e2e and its before/after screenshots above. Fixes #92122

target.title: fix(doctor): surface multi-account default routing warnings in preview and lint
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` preview and `openclaw doctor --lint` did not surface warnings
about multi-account channels that lack explicit default routing or complete
account-scoped bindings, and an earlier revision of this PR introduced a
**repair-mode regression**: `openclaw doctor --fix` silently dropped the
multi-account default-routing warning that `main` prints today.

Root cause of the regression: the `default-account-routing` check is a
**detection-only** core health check — it reports through `result.findings`, not
`result.changes`/`result.warnings`. The repair helper that routes it through
gateway-services (`runCoreContributionHealthRepair`) rendered only `changes` and
`warnings` and never rendered `findings`. Because this PR also removed the direct
`doctor-config-flow` emission, the warning disappeared entirely in `--fix` mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surface `collectMissingDefaultAccountBindingWarnings` and
`collectMissingExplicitDefaultAccountWarnings` through one structured check
(`core/doctor/default-account-routing`) across all three doctor modes — preview
(`collectDoctorPreviewNotes`), lint (`healthCheckIds`), and repair
(`runCoreContributionHealthRepair` inside `runGatewayServicesHealth`) — and
delete the duplicate direct calls from `doctor-config-flow`. Single source of
truth, no second emission path.

The repair-mode fix renders findings using the **existing** canonical renderer
the structured contribution path already uses (`renderStructuredHealthFindings`),
so `--fix` keeps printing the warning that `main` shows. The render is **scoped to
detection-only checks** (those with no `repair`): `runCoreContributionHealthRepair`
is also used for the repair-capable `browser-clawd-profile-residue` check, whose
pre-repair finding stays in `result.findings` after a successful archive — so
rendering *all* findings would make `--fix` warn about residue it just repaired.
Gating the render on `checks.every(check => check.repair === undefined)` surfaces
default-account-routing while leaving the browser path's output unchanged (both
call sites pass a single check, so the batch guard is exact). The check stays
detection-only (no
auto-rewrite of operator config); `--fix` reports the warning, it does not mutate
routing.

## User Impact

Operators running `openclaw doctor` (preview), `openclaw doctor --lint`, or
`openclaw doctor --fix` on a multi-account channel with no explicit default now
see the same default-routing warnings in **all three** modes. `--lint` reports a
warning-severity finding (nonzero exit, consistent with existing
warning-severity lint checks); no config is rewritten.

## Evidence

All proof is real `openclaw doctor` CLI output against a representative
multi-account config plus a unit-level output assertion with a negative control.
No live gateway or secrets required — the warning is driven purely by config
shape.

**Config used** (`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`), a telegram channel with two accounts
and no `accounts.default`, channel-only binding:

```json
{
  "channels": { "telegram": { "accounts": { "alerts": {}, "work": {} } } },
  "bindings": [{ "agentId": "ops", "match": { "channel": "telegram" } }]
}
```

### 1. Real CLI — `doctor` preview surfaces the findings

```
$ openclaw doctor --non-interactive   # preview notes path (collectDoctorPreviewNotes)
◇  Doctor warnings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid          │
│    account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts,       │
│    work). Channel-only bindings (no accountId) match only default. Add  │
│    bindings[].match.accountId for one of these accounts (or "*"), or    │
│    add channels.telegram.accounts.default.                              │
│  - channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit  │
│    default is set. Set channels.telegram.defaultAccount or add          │
│    channels.telegram.accounts.default to avoid fallback routing.        │
```

### 2. Real CLI — `doctor --lint` surfaces the findings

```
$ openclaw doctor --lint --json   # exit 1
core/doctor/default-account-routing | warning | channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts, work). ...
core/doctor/default-account-routing | warning | channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit default is set. Set channels.telegram.defaultAccount or add channels.telegram.accounts.default ...
```

### 3. Real CLI — `doctor --fix` surfaces the findings (the regression fix)

```
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing - channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts, work). ...
[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing - channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit default is set. ...
```

### 4. Real CLI — negative control (proves the fix is load-bearing)

Rebuilt `dist` with the `renderStructuredHealthFindings(ctx, result.findings)`
line removed, then re-ran the same `doctor --fix`:

```
# count of rendered "[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing" lines in --fix
without the findings render:  0    <- regression reproduced (warning silently dropped)
with the findings render:     2    <- fixed
```

### 5. Unit — output assertion + negative control

`doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` → "renders default-account-routing
findings in gateway-services repair mode" asserts the warning **text reaches
`ctx.runtime.log`** in `--fix` mode (not merely that the repair runner was
called):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  50 passed (50)
```

Two negative controls prove both halves of the fix:

- Remove the findings render → the detection-only test FAILS
  (`Number of calls: 0`) — guards the dropped-warning regression.
- Render *all* `result.findings` instead of filtering to detection-only checks →
  the new test "does not re-render a repairable check's pre-repair findings in fix
  mode" FAILS — guards against warning about `browser-clawd-profile-residue` that
  `--fix` just archived (the over-render this PR avoids).

### 6. Adjacent suites green

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  17 passed (17)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/preview-warnings.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  44 passed (44)
```

Core change is small: a `checks.every(check => check.repair === undefined)` guard
around the findings render in `runCoreContributionHealthRepair`, plus wiring
`core/doctor/default-account-routing` into the gateway-services contribution and
removing the now-duplicate direct emission from `doctor-config-flow`. No new
config/env surface, no schema change, no data migration.

---

🤖 AI-assisted: implementation and proof harness authored with AI assistance;
all code, tests, and the real-environment CLI proof were reviewed and run
locally by the author.

target.title: fix(agents): bound body-less MCP HTTP text responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`ensureGlobalFetchResponse` in the MCP HTTP fetch wrapper previously read body-less `Response`-like objects via `await response.text()`. That compatibility path exists so the MCP SDK can parse OAuth error text from foreign response implementations, but a body-less response with no reliable size signal can otherwise force OpenClaw to allocate an unbounded string.

This PR makes that body-less fallback policy explicit: text-only foreign responses are preserved only when they advertise a safe decimal `Content-Length`; missing, malformed, invalid, or oversized lengths fail closed before calling `text()`.

## Changes

- `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.ts`
  - Adds `MCP_HTTP_MAX_TEXT_RESPONSE_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024`.
  - Parses `Content-Length` for body-less foreign responses.
  - Accepts only trimmed decimal digit `Content-Length` values before converting to a safe integer.
  - Returns `new Response(null, init)` without calling `response.text()` when `Content-Length` is missing, malformed, invalid, negative, or over the cap.
  - Preserves small body-less OAuth error text only when the declared length is within the cap.
  - Keeps a post-read UTF-8 byte-length check as defense in depth if the declared length lies.
- `src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts`
  - Keeps MCP SDK OAuth parsing coverage for small body-less error text with safe `Content-Length`.
  - Adds coverage that declared-oversized body-less responses do not call `text()`.
  - Adds coverage that no-`Content-Length` body-less responses do not call `text()`.
  - Adds coverage that malformed non-decimal `Content-Length` values (`1e3`, `0x40`) do not call `text()`.
  - Adds coverage that declared-small but actually oversized text is dropped after the post-read UTF-8 byte check.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: A body-less MCP HTTP foreign response with missing, malformed, or oversized `Content-Length` must not call `text()` at all; the wrapper should preserve status/headers and return `body=null`.
- **Real environment tested**: Local Node v22 workspace, real `http.createServer`, production `buildMcpHttpFetch`, and a custom FetchLike adapter that converts the real HTTP response into the MCP body-less foreign-response shape.
- **Exact steps**: A local HTTP server returned a 1 MiB + 1 byte body. The proof called production `buildMcpHttpFetch` for both `/declared-large` and `/no-length`; the adapter counted calls to the foreign response `text()` method.
- **Observed result after fix**: both responses returned status 400 with `body=null`, and `textCalls=0`.
- **What was not tested**: A live external MCP OAuth server was not hit; this proof uses a local loopback server plus the same production MCP fetch wrapper and body-less foreign-response contract.

Loopback proof output:

```json
{"declared":{"status":400,"body":null},"unbounded":{"status":400,"body":null},"textCalls":0,"declaredTextCalls":0}
```

## Current status proof

- **Current head**: `8bb30cd79ae192d15c86deb10165d12ba450e8ca`.
- **Current GitHub PR diff**: `+160/-2 (2 files)`.
- **Current changed files**:

```text
src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts
src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.ts
```

- **Malformed length proof added**: focused regression coverage now proves `Content-Length: 1e3` and `Content-Length: 0x40` return `body=null` without calling `text()`.

## Compatibility / Policy Note

This PR intentionally changes no-`Content-Length` body-less text-only MCP OAuth errors from readable text to `body=null`. That is the fail-closed option from #97521. Maintainer/security review still needs to accept that policy before merge.

For declared-small body-less responses, the only available API is `text()`, so the implementation trusts a syntactically valid decimal `Content-Length` before reading and then verifies the returned UTF-8 byte length. The regression test covers a lying response that declares `Content-Length: 64` but returns more than 1 MiB; the wrapper drops it after the post-read check. Fully avoiding allocation for that lying declared-small shape would require failing closed for all body-less text responses, including the current OAuth compatibility case.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest after rejecting malformed `Content-Length` values:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts --run

Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

target.title: fix(agents): classify upstream_error as fallbackable to harden model fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95519. When a primary model's provider returns an error with `type: "upstream_error"` (the OpenAI-compatible "the upstream backend failed" shape, e.g. `{"error":{"message":"Upstream request failed","type":"upstream_error","param":"","code":null}}`), OpenClaw ends the turn with `LLM request failed` instead of trying the configured `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`. The trajectory shows only the primary model, no `model.fallback_step` event, and no fallback attempt.

Root cause is a classification gap. The provider error surfaces as an assistant message with `stopReason: "error"` and `errorType: "upstream_error"`. The embedded runner's assistant-stage failover gate (`run.ts` calls `isFailoverAssistantError` / `classifyAssistantFailoverReason`) is what decides whether to throw a `FailoverError` into the model-fallback loop. `classifyAssistantFailoverReason` runs `classifyFailoverSignal`, and nothing mapped `upstream_error` to a failover reason:

- `upstream_error` is lowercase `snake_case`, so it was not recognized as a transient provider type, and
- the message text `Upstream request failed` matches no transient classifier, and
- there is no recognized HTTP status in this payload to fall back on.

So the gate returned `null` ("not a failover error"), the assistant stage took the `continue_normal` path instead of throwing, and the run returned a terminal error payload (`non_deliverable_terminal_turn`) that the model-fallback loop treats as a successful result — the fallback chain never runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix classifies `upstream_error` as a transient, fallbackable reason at the point the signal is built, so the existing assistant-stage failover machinery throws a `FailoverError` and the model-fallback loop advances to the next configured model — the same path already used for Codex `server_error` (`run.codex-server-error-fallback.test.ts`).

Three changes in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` and `src/agents/failover-error.ts`:

1. New `classifyFailoverReasonFromErrorType` in `errors.ts`, run early in `classifyFailoverSignal` (before message/status classification): `upstream_error → timeout`, `server_error → server_error`; unknown types return `null` and fall through. This is the change that fixes #95519, because `buildAssistantFailoverSignal` passes the assistant message's `errorType` straight into `classifyFailoverSignal`, so the gate now recognizes `upstream_error`.
2. `isStableProviderErrorType` in `failover-error.ts` now also accepts `lowercase_snake_case` (in addition to `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`). This only affects `readDirectErrorType`, used by the thrown-error coercion path (`resolveFailoverReasonFromError`), so a thrown `upstream_error` payload is also extractable. The generic-type exclusion list (`api_error`, `server_error`, etc.) is unchanged.
3. `API_ERROR_TRANSIENT_SIGNALS_RE` matches `upstream.error`, so both `upstream error` and `upstream_error` are caught in the message-text path used for `api_error`-typed payloads (defense-in-depth).

Non-transient types (auth, context overflow, validation) are unaffected and continue to return `null`.

## User Impact

With `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` configured, a primary-model `upstream_error` is now treated as a fallbackable failure: the run throws a `FailoverError`, the model-fallback loop skips the failed candidate and tries the next model, and the trajectory records a fallback step. If all candidates fail, the user gets a `FallbackSummaryError` with per-attempt detail instead of the generic `LLM request failed`. No behavior change when no fallback is configured, and no change for non-transient errors.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage in `src/agents/failover-error.test.ts`, including a test that drives the **exact production gate** the runtime uses (`classifyAssistantFailoverReason` / `isFailoverAssistantError`) with the #95519 assistant-message shape (`stopReason: "error"`, `errorType: "upstream_error"`, message `Upstream request failed`, no HTTP status). This message returns `null` from the gate without the fix (verified: message-only `classifyFailoverSignal` is `null`) and `timeout` with it, so it is a true regression test of the runtime path — not just an isolated signal-classifier call.

Command:

```
pnpm test src/agents/failover-error.test.ts
```

Result:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  97 passed (97)
   Duration  565ms
```

New/relevant cases:

```
✓ upstream_error type triggers fallback > classifies upstream_error errorType as timeout (fallbackable)
✓ upstream_error type triggers fallback > classifies server_error errorType as server_error (fallbackable)
✓ upstream_error type triggers fallback > resolves upstream_error via resolveFailoverReasonFromError with nested payload
✓ upstream_error type triggers fallback > does not classify unknown errorType as fallbackable
✓ upstream_error type triggers fallback > classifies upstream_error via JSON api_error transient signals (regex)
✓ upstream_error type triggers fallback > treats an upstream_error assistant message as fallbackable at the production gate
```

No-regression check on the adjacent failover surfaces the change touches:

```
pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/result-fallback-classifier.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  47 passed (47)
```

The transport layer already extracts a nested provider `type` into `errorType` (proven for the identical code path by the `rate_limit_error` case in `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts`), which is how `errorType: "upstream_error"` reaches the gate above.

target.title: fix(doctor): surface multi-account default routing warnings in preview and lint
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` preview and `openclaw doctor --lint` did not surface warnings
about multi-account channels that lack explicit default routing or complete
account-scoped bindings, and an earlier revision of this PR introduced a
**repair-mode regression**: `openclaw doctor --fix` silently dropped the
multi-account default-routing warning that `main` prints today.

Root cause of the regression: the `default-account-routing` check is a
**detection-only** core health check — it reports through `result.findings`, not
`result.changes`/`result.warnings`. The repair helper that routes it through
gateway-services (`runCoreContributionHealthRepair`) rendered only `changes` and
`warnings` and never rendered `findings`. Because this PR also removed the direct
`doctor-config-flow` emission, the warning disappeared entirely in `--fix` mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surface `collectMissingDefaultAccountBindingWarnings` and
`collectMissingExplicitDefaultAccountWarnings` through one structured check
(`core/doctor/default-account-routing`) across all three doctor modes — preview
(`collectDoctorPreviewNotes`), lint (`healthCheckIds`), and repair
(`runCoreContributionHealthRepair` inside `runGatewayServicesHealth`) — and
delete the duplicate direct calls from `doctor-config-flow`. Single source of
truth, no second emission path.

The repair-mode fix renders findings using the **existing** canonical renderer
the structured contribution path already uses (`renderStructuredHealthFindings`),
so `--fix` keeps printing the warning that `main` shows. The render is **scoped to
detection-only checks** (those with no `repair`): `runCoreContributionHealthRepair`
is also used for the repair-capable `browser-clawd-profile-residue` check, whose
pre-repair finding stays in `result.findings` after a successful archive — so
rendering *all* findings would make `--fix` warn about residue it just repaired.
Gating the render on `checks.every(check => check.repair === undefined)` surfaces
default-account-routing while leaving the browser path's output unchanged (both
call sites pass a single check, so the batch guard is exact). The check stays
detection-only (no
auto-rewrite of operator config); `--fix` reports the warning, it does not mutate
routing.

## User Impact

Operators running `openclaw doctor` (preview), `openclaw doctor --lint`, or
`openclaw doctor --fix` on a multi-account channel with no explicit default now
see the same default-routing warnings in **all three** modes. `--lint` reports a
warning-severity finding (nonzero exit, consistent with existing
warning-severity lint checks); no config is rewritten.

## Evidence

All proof is real `openclaw doctor` CLI output against a representative
multi-account config plus a unit-level output assertion with a negative control.
No live gateway or secrets required — the warning is driven purely by config
shape.

**Config used** (`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`), a telegram channel with two accounts
and no `accounts.default`, channel-only binding:

```json
{
  "channels": { "telegram": { "accounts": { "alerts": {}, "work": {} } } },
  "bindings": [{ "agentId": "ops", "match": { "channel": "telegram" } }]
}
```

### 1. Real CLI — `doctor` preview surfaces the findings

```
$ openclaw doctor --non-interactive   # preview notes path (collectDoctorPreviewNotes)
◇  Doctor warnings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid          │
│    account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts,       │
│    work). Channel-only bindings (no accountId) match only default. Add  │
│    bindings[].match.accountId for one of these accounts (or "*"), or    │
│    add channels.telegram.accounts.default.                              │
│  - channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit  │
│    default is set. Set channels.telegram.defaultAccount or add          │
│    channels.telegram.accounts.default to avoid fallback routing.        │
```

### 2. Real CLI — `doctor --lint` surfaces the findings

```
$ openclaw doctor --lint --json   # exit 1
core/doctor/default-account-routing | warning | channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts, work). ...
core/doctor/default-account-routing | warning | channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit default is set. Set channels.telegram.defaultAccount or add channels.telegram.accounts.default ...
```

### 3. Real CLI — `doctor --fix` surfaces the findings (the regression fix)

```
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing - channels.telegram: accounts.default is missing and no valid account-scoped binding exists for configured accounts (alerts, work). ...
[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing - channels.telegram: multiple accounts are configured but no explicit default is set. ...
```

### 4. Real CLI — negative control (proves the fix is load-bearing)

Rebuilt `dist` with the `renderStructuredHealthFindings(ctx, result.findings)`
line removed, then re-ran the same `doctor --fix`:

```
# count of rendered "[warning] core/doctor/default-account-routing" lines in --fix
without the findings render:  0    <- regression reproduced (warning silently dropped)
with the findings render:     2    <- fixed
```

### 5. Unit — output assertion + negative control

`doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` → "renders default-account-routing
findings in gateway-services repair mode" asserts the warning **text reaches
`ctx.runtime.log`** in `--fix` mode (not merely that the repair runner was
called):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  50 passed (50)
```

Two negative controls prove both halves of the fix:

- Remove the findings render → the detection-only test FAILS
  (`Number of calls: 0`) — guards the dropped-warning regression.
- Render *all* `result.findings` instead of filtering to detection-only checks →
  the new test "does not re-render a repairable check's pre-repair findings in fix
  mode" FAILS — guards against warning about `browser-clawd-profile-residue` that
  `--fix` just archived (the over-render this PR avoids).

### 6. Adjacent suites green

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  17 passed (17)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/preview-warnings.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  44 passed (44)
```

Core change is small: a `checks.every(check => check.repair === undefined)` guard
around the findings render in `runCoreContributionHealthRepair`, plus wiring
`core/doctor/default-account-routing` into the gateway-services contribution and
removing the now-duplicate direct emission from `doctor-config-flow`. No new
config/env surface, no schema change, no data migration.

---

🤖 AI-assisted: implementation and proof harness authored with AI assistance;
all code, tests, and the real-environment CLI proof were reviewed and run
locally by the author.

target.title: Skip QMD memory search when scope denies
target.body:
## Summary

- short-circuit QMD-backed `memory_search` when the current session is denied by `memory.qmd.scope`
- return an empty successful result with `debug.skipped = "skipped_by_scope"` instead of opening the memory manager
- keep the QMD manager's own scope guard as defense in depth, but log it as `skipped_by_scope` at debug level instead of a warning-style denial

## Why

Denied QMD memory searches are correctly blocked today, but the request can still reach the QMD manager in channel/thread contexts that are outside scope. This creates noisy `qmd search denied by scope` journal entries and can waste work before the denial is known.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts extensions/memory-core/src/tools.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory-tool-manager-mock.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.test.ts`

target.title: fix(proxy): apply enhanced NO_PROXY matching to global undici dispatcher (fixes #95998)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95998.

When `HTTPS_PROXY` is set, the global EnvHttpProxyAgent routes ALL requests through the proxy — including internal plugin requests that should bypass via `NO_PROXY`. The built-in undici NO_PROXY matcher does not support leading-dot subdomain patterns, CIDR notation, or octet wildcards.

OpenClaw already has `matchesNoProxy()` that handles these — but it was only used by provider helpers, not the global dispatcher.

## Changes Made

1. **NO_PROXY-aware proxy dispatcher** — Wraps every EnvHttpProxyAgent with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before dispatching to the direct bypass agent.

2. **Lifecycle synchronization (P1 fix)** — Promise-style `close()`/`destroy()` now await both the bypass agent AND the proxy dispatcher before settling. `destroy(err)` arguments are forwarded correctly.

3. **no_proxy precedence (P1 fix)** — Empty lowercase `no_proxy` now correctly shadows uppercase `NO_PROXY`, matching undici EnvHttpProxyAgent semantics.

## Network Boundary Change — Scope and Rationale

This PR extends OpenClaw existing `matchesNoProxy()` (already used by provider helpers) to the global undici dispatcher. This means NO_PROXY patterns that undici built-in matcher cannot handle (CIDR, octet-wildcard) will now correctly bypass the proxy at the process level.

- **Scope**: Only affects the NO_PROXY matching path. The EnvHttpProxyAgent is still used for all non-bypassed requests. Bypass agent inherits the same timeout/connect policy.
- **Risk**: `matchesNoProxy()` is already proven in production via provider helpers. This PR applies the same logic to the global dispatcher.
- **Upgrade**: Existing deployments with basic domain NO_PROXY patterns are unaffected. Deployments using CIDR or octet-wildcard entries will see those patterns start working (previously broken).
- **Lifecycle safety**: close/destroy synchronizes both dispatchers. Promise-style and callback-style both work correctly.

## Evidence

**Enhanced matcher proof (18/18 tests passed):**
```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx _matcher_proof.mjs

=== Enhanced NO_PROXY Matcher Proof ===
(Core of PR #97713 — the dispatcher wrapper uses matchesNoProxy())

  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, matching: true
  ✅ Basic: NO_PROXY=example.com, non-matching: false
  ✅ Subdomain: .myqcloud.com, COS bucket: true
```

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/proxy-env.test.ts

      Tests  55 passed (55)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/net/undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

## AI Assistance

- AI-assisted: Yes
- Manually reviewed and verified

## False Positive Risk Mitigation

The enhanced NO_PROXY matcher (`matchesNoProxy()`) is already used by provider helpers in production — this PR extends the same proven logic to the global dispatcher. The false positive risk is inherently limited because:

1. **Pattern-gated**: The enhanced matcher only triggers when the NO_PROXY value actually contains CIDR, octet-wildcard, or leading-dot patterns. For plain domain matching, the behavior is identical to undici built-in.
2. **Already deployed**: Provider helpers (SSRF guard, per-request routing) have used `matchesNoProxy()` in production without incident.
3. **Conservative**: The bypass agent inherits the same timeout and connect policy as the EnvHttpProxyAgent, so bypassed requests behave identically to proxied ones — just without the proxy hop.
4. **Auditable**: The `matchesNoProxy()` logic is contained in a single function (`src/infra/net/proxy-env.ts`) and is covered by 55 unit tests.

Maintainers should explicitly accept the broader proxy-bypass boundary before merge (see Network Boundary section above).


## Proof of Global Dispatcher Routing

The PR changes the global undici dispatcher by wrapping it with a Proxy that checks `matchesNoProxy()` before routing. Each dispatched request follows this flow:

1. `dispatch()` is called on the Proxy wrapper
2. If `hasEnvHttpProxyAgentConfigured() && matchesNoProxy(origin)` → route through **bypass Agent** (direct, no proxy)
3. Otherwise → route through **EnvHttpProxyAgent** (through proxy)

This logic is verified by:

- **35 dispatcher tests** — `undici-global-dispatcher.test.ts` covers proxy wrapper creation, dispatch routing, lifecycle sync, and bypass agent behavior
- **55 proxy-env tests** — `proxy-env.test.ts` covers all `matchesNoProxy()` patterns (CIDR, octet-wildcard, subdomain, precedence)
- **18 matcher scenarios** — verified individually with terminal output above

The 90 unit tests run against the actual undici runtime and confirm the wrapper correctly:
- Forwards matching requests to the bypass agent
- Forwards non-matching requests to the EnvHttpProxyAgent
- Synchronizes close/destroy lifecycle
- Preserves `no_proxy` precedence


## Live Proxy Proof

A local HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1:18999 was configured as HTTPS_PROXY. The NO_PROXY-aware dispatcher was set as the global undici dispatcher, then fetch() requests were made under different NO_PROXY settings. The proxy logged every CONNECT attempt.

```
1. Without NO_PROXY:
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

2. NO_PROXY=example.com (matching):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://example.com)  ← intercepted

3. NO_PROXY=other.com (non-matching):
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443  ← all through proxy
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443
  [proxy] CONNECT example.com:443

4. NO_PROXY=100.64.0.0/10 (CIDR — undici lacks this):
  → BYPASS (NO_PROXY match: https://100.100.0.1)  ← CIDR works
```

target.title: feat(control-ui): session grouping with drag & drop and channel categorization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI sessions table is a flat list. Once an operator runs many sessions across agents and message channels (Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, ...), there is no way to organize them: no grouping, no way to categorize channel-originated sessions, and no equivalent of the desktop app's custom session groups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a persistent per-session `category` field end-to-end (gateway protocol `sessions.patch` -> session store -> list rows -> live session-change events) and a "Group by" control on the web Sessions page with None / Custom groups / Channel / Kind / Agent / Date modes. The field is named `category` to stay clearly separate from the existing chat-group concepts (`groupId`, `groupChannel`, kind `group`). Custom group membership persists server-side on the session entry; empty just-created groups live in browser localStorage until a session is assigned. Cleared categories emit an explicit `null` in session events so other connected clients drop the group during merge-reconcile instead of going stale.

## User Impact

- Group the sessions table by custom groups, channel, kind, agent, or date, with section headers and counts; the chosen mode persists per browser.
- Create custom groups and assign sessions by dragging rows onto a section (drop-target highlight), or via a per-row group selector; sessions from message channels can be categorized like any other session.
- Channel mode buckets sessions by their originating channel out of the box.
- Group names are searchable in the table filter and shown in the session details panel.
- Protocol change is additive: `sessions.patch` accepts `category: string | null`; session rows and change events carry `category`.

## Evidence

- Backend: `sessions-patch` suite 239 passed (new category persist/trim/clear/duplicate/empty tests), `server.sessions.list-changed` 46 passed after the event payload change, protocol + session-utils + store-rpc 690 passed.
- UI: 42 tests passed, including new coverage for grouping helpers (channel/agent/date/category bucketing, group ordering), section headers and counts, drag-drop assignment via header drop targets, the filtered empty state under active grouping, and reconcile dropping a cleared category.
- `tsgo` core and UI lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files.
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.5) over four rounds; the three accepted findings (blank empty state when grouped, `agent:main:main` misgrouped in Agent mode, stale category on other clients after clear) were fixed with regression tests; final run reported no actionable findings.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui.md` describes the new grouping behavior.

target.title: fix(ios): restore in-flight runs after reconnect
target.body:
Part of #100197. Supersedes the stacked `afterSeq` design in #100267.

## What Problem This Solves

When iOS backgrounds, reconnects, changes sessions, or misses an event sequence, it can lose ownership of a run that is still active on the Gateway. The transcript may look idle, Abort disappears, and a second send becomes possible while the first run is still working.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already exposes the canonical active-run snapshot through `chat.history.inFlightRun`; the TUI already consumes that contract. This rewrite removes every proposed `afterSeq` protocol/client change and restores ownership from the existing snapshot instead.

The shared Apple chat model now:

- adopts active run ID and buffered text during bootstrap, foreground resume, sequence-gap recovery, immediate post-send refresh, delayed retries, and completion refreshes;
- orders history snapshots against newer live deltas, terminal events, session messages, session switches, agent changes, and concurrent history requests;
- keeps ownership stable when another client streams a different run in the same session;
- scopes bare-global/default-agent aliases and non-default agent-qualified global sessions without cross-agent transcript adoption;
- distinguishes current Gateway negative state via `sessionInfo.hasActiveRun` from legacy gateways that omit active-run metadata;
- preserves live/provisional transcript rows when delayed history arrives, including identical replies from different turns;
- rearms timeouts safely and clears silent completed/failed runs from authoritative current-Gateway state.

Codex app-server source confirms a turn becomes `InProgress` with no message items before later `AgentMessageDelta` notifications (`codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359`). That is why an active run with an empty buffered string is still valid ownership.

## User Impact

Returning to iOS or macOS chat no longer loses an active response. Streaming text, tool state, Abort, and the send lock recover without adding a Gateway protocol or cursor, while older Gateways retain the prior transcript-based completion fallback.

## Evidence

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests` — 129/129 passed after rebase, including unrelated session activity without a chat-run snapshot.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos` — passed after rebase.
- SwiftFormat lint with `config/swiftformat` — clean for every touched Swift file.
- Final full-branch Codex autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings after separating session-wide activity from chat-run ownership.
- Direct Gateway contract review: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`, `src/gateway/server-session-events.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/session-active-runs.ts`.
- Direct Codex contract review at `be33f80bc65159c094ecd06bf155afa3061ce23d`: `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155-183`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359-367`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs:375-378`.

Visual reconnect/background proof is requested separately on this exact head.

target.title: fix compaction timeout partial progress
target.body:
## Summary

- Preserve completed chunk summaries when a later compaction chunk times out, so timeout recovery can reuse partial progress instead of falling back to a generic “summary unavailable” note and restarting from chunk 1 on the next attempt.
- Preserve cooperative partial progress through the outer `compactWithSafetyTimeout()` wall-clock timeout path by allowing the canceled native compaction to settle with its cancellation-produced result before the timeout error wins the race.
- Wire the safety-timeout reason through the real native `activeSession.compact()` / `activeSession.abortCompaction(reason)` path, so `AgentSession` can commit a result that was produced by timeout cancellation while still treating non-timeout aborts as cancellation.
- Keep the timeout-result acceptance window alive through the native `AgentSession` post-await commit continuation, then expire it once the safety wrapper rejects so a late-settling timeout-aborted compaction cannot append session state after the run is already failed.
- Remove the old `src/node-host/with-timeout.ts` helper after this compaction path stopped using it, which fixes the `check-dependencies` deadcode CI failure for the updated branch.
- Keep caller abort cancellation semantics intact: non-timeout aborts still do not get converted into successful partial summaries.
- Surface compaction timeout details in the preflight failure reply, including the existing `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds` knob, while generic non-verbose compaction failures still hide details.

Fixes #92043

## Maintainer-ready notes

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users with large transcripts can hit the default compaction wall-clock timeout after some chunks already summarized successfully. Before this patch, that useful progress was discarded and the next attempt repeated the same earlier chunks, creating a permanent failure loop. The preflight reply also hid that the failure was a timeout, leaving users without the relevant config knob.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause reliability fix for compaction timeout progress reuse and timeout failure copy.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the local source/runtime surface covered here. The change has RED/GREEN regression coverage for inner chunk timeout, outer safety-timeout cancellation, and user-facing timeout copy; it preserves abort cancellation behavior and does not alter default timeout values or public config shape.
- **Root cause:** The root source was split across three timeout boundaries. `summarizeChunks()` discarded completed chunk summaries on timeout-shaped failures; the outer `compactWithSafetyTimeout()` could reject with its wall-clock timeout before a cooperating native compaction returned the partial result it produced during timeout cancellation; the real native `AgentSession` path aborted compaction without preserving the timeout reason, so a result produced after timeout cancellation was still classified as plain aborted work; the timeout-abort classification originally accepted any matching error name, which left a late-settling timeout result able to append after the safety wrapper had already rejected; and the first bounded-acceptance implementation expired the token before `AgentSession`'s post-await commit gate could observe it.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** This changes the owners that enforce the partial-progress invariant: `src/agents/compaction.ts` carries partial summaries from inner chunk failures, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-safety-timeout.ts` preserves the timeout reason, gives the native post-await commit continuation a bounded chance to return cancellation-produced progress before the timeout rejection wins, and expires timeout-result acceptance once the wrapper rejects; `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` commits a compact result only while that timeout reason is still accepted instead of accepting arbitrary late timeout-named aborts. The copy change stays at the preflight compaction failure formatter.
- **What did NOT change:** Chunk planning, model retry policy, compaction timeout defaults, persistent session storage, provider routing, public config shape, and unrelated compaction behavior are unchanged and out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/agents/compaction.ts` remains the source-of-truth owner for summary partial-progress behavior, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-safety-timeout.ts` owns the native compaction wall-clock race, and `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` remains the source-of-truth owner for preflight agent-run failure copy.
- **Patch quality notes:** Timeout recovery is bounded to cooperative cancellation settlement at the timeout boundary and to the active safety-wrapper acceptance window through the native commit continuation. Non-timeout aborts still reject promptly, non-settling compactions still reject with `Compaction timed out`, late timeout-aborted results after wrapper rejection are ignored by `AgentSession`, and the default 180s timeout is unchanged.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/compaction-partial-summary.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.compaction-safety-timeout.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts`, and `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Regression test scenarios: a two-chunk compaction where chunk 1 succeeds and chunk 2 throws `TimeoutError` must return the chunk 1 summary plus a `[Partial summary: ...]` marker; a compaction canceled by outer timeout and immediately resolving with progress must return that progress instead of `Compaction timed out`; direct native compaction passes the safety timeout reason into `activeSession.abortCompaction(reason)` so timeout-aborted results can be committed only while the safety wrapper still accepts that reason; a late result after wrapper rejection must not remain accepted; a preflight compaction timeout must surface the timeout reason and config guidance.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The regression tests exercise the source owner boundaries directly and keep existing abort/timeout tests in place so timeout recovery cannot convert user cancellation or hung compaction into success.
- **Out of scope:** This PR does not change the default 180s timeout, add persistent checkpoint storage, change the shape/default of `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds`, alter compaction chunk planning, or change model/provider retry policy.

## Root Cause

`src/agents/compaction.ts` treated timeout errors the same as cancellation and rethrew immediately before attaching the already-generated summary to the error. `summarizeWithFallback()` therefore had no partial summary to reuse, even when earlier chunks had already completed successfully.

The outer safety timeout added a second loss path: `compactWithSafetyTimeout()` raced native compaction against a timeout rejection. On timeout it aborted the active compaction, but the timeout rejection could win before the native compaction settled with the partial result it produced during that cancellation.

The native caller added a third loss path: `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirectOnce()` canceled the real `AgentSession` via `activeSession.abortCompaction()` with no timeout reason, and `AgentSession.runCompactionWork()` discarded any compact result once its internal compaction signal was aborted. Timeout cancellation and user/request abort therefore collapsed into the same aborted state.

Separately, `buildPreflightCompactionFailureText()` hid the preflight compaction reason unless verbose details were enabled. That made a 180s compaction timeout look like a generic unrecoverable compaction failure and did not point users at the configured timeout knob.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Later chunk timeout and outer wall-clock safety timeout no longer discard already-generated compaction summary progress; preflight compaction timeout replies now show the timeout reason and `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds` guidance.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw worktrees. Original wall-clock/runtime proof was collected on `/media/vdc/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-92043`, branch `feat/issue-92043`; latest conflict-resolution verification was collected on `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-92899`, head `6b283d6f88045481f98530d23405f56dc6725799` after rebasing through `origin/main` `cd305b3b0cb9fcedaccfd5cec3b0ced1fde032ce`; latest `daily_fix.sh check-main-drift` required `sync-main` because `origin/main` had advanced 241 commits with overlapping compaction/session files, and the conflict was resolved locally before validation.

target.title: feat(ui): scroll truncated sidebar session names on hover
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long session titles in the Control UI sidebar's recent-sessions list get clipped with an ellipsis, and there is no way to read the hidden tail without opening the session or waiting for the native tooltip. Titles like "Fix stale iMessage group-allowlist warning copy" become indistinguishable once several sessions share a prefix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hovering a session row now animates the truncated label so the clipped tail scrolls into view (marquee-style), and the label snaps back quickly when the pointer leaves. The animation transitions `text-indent` rather than transforming an inner wrapper because `text-overflow` renders no ellipsis for atomic inline children — the wrapper approach would have lost the resting "…". Scroll duration is proportional to the hidden distance (80px/s, 300ms minimum) so short and long titles both stay readable, labels that fit are left untouched, and `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps the static ellipsis. The helper (`ui/src/lib/hover-marquee.ts`) plus generic `.hover-marquee` CSS are reusable for other truncated labels (e.g. the sessions table or session picker) as follow-ups; this PR wires only the requested sidebar surface.

## User Impact

Hovering a truncated session name in the sidebar scrolls the full title into view; moving the mouse away restores the normal ellipsized label. No behavior change for labels that fit, keyboard users, or reduced-motion users.

## Evidence

- Rest (ellipsis preserved): ![rest](https://github.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/releases/download/sidebar-hover-marquee/marquee-rest.png)

target.title: fix(agents): suppress unhandled rejection from async abort callback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the agent session extension abort callback called `session.abort()` asynchronously and ignored the returned promise. If `session.abort()` ever rejects (for example due to a future regression in run shutdown or an extension-provided abort path that delegates here), the rejection would become an unhandled rejection and could crash the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a `.catch()` handler to the fire-and-forget `this.abort()` call in the extension abort callback. The handler writes a generic stderr diagnostic (`agent-session: extension abort failed`) so the failure is observable without propagating as an unhandled rejection, while avoiding the leak of provider or config details that a raw error might carry. This is defense-in-depth: current `Agent.waitForIdle()` normally resolves the active run promise, so the rejecting path is not reproducible under normal runtime conditions, but the callback boundary is now guarded against future regressions.

## User Impact

Extension abort handling is more resilient; a rare or future abort failure is logged to stderr instead of surfacing as an unhandled rejection that could terminate the session or process.

target.title: fix(twitch): channel status keeps reporting connected after the chat transport drops
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Twitch channel keeps reporting a live connection after
its chat transport has actually dropped. Once the initial connection succeeds,
`openclaw channels status` (and the Control UI) shows the account as running
indefinitely even if the underlying chat socket is later disconnected by a
network blip, a Twitch-side close, or a failed auto-reconnect. Because the
channel never reported a transport-level `connected` state, the shared channel
health monitor also could not detect the dead transport to restart it, so a
silently disconnected Twitch account would stay dark with no operator signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

Twitch set `running: true` on start but only cleared status on a connect-time
failure or a manual stop; the sole `onDisconnect` listener lived inside the
connect handshake and unbound as soon as authentication settled, so no listener
survived to observe a later disconnect. This change registers a persistent
`onConnect`/`onDisconnect` pair on the chat client and feeds a distinct
`connected` flag (plus `lastTransportActivityAt`) through the monitor's status
sink, surfacing it in the channel status summary. `running` is deliberately
left owned by the monitor lifecycle and stays `true` across transient
reconnects — the same split the qqbot channel adopted in #100127. This restores
the `connected` / `lastTransportActivityAt` signals the shared health monitor
(`evaluateChannelHealth`) needs to notice and recover a dead Twitch transport.

The other bundled channels (Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Feishu, Matrix,
WhatsApp, Telegram, and the webhook-based channels) already clear their
connection status on transport close, and the probe-based channels compute
liveness on demand — Twitch was the remaining channel that latched a live
status and never cleared it. The on-demand `probeTwitch` check is a separate,
independent throwaway-client credential test; it does not observe the live
monitor's chat client and the health monitor does not consult it, so the
persistent `connected` wiring is still required.

## User Impact

Operators running Twitch now see the account flip to disconnected in
`openclaw channels status` when its chat transport actually drops, instead of a
permanently green status. This also lets the channel health monitor detect and
restart a dead Twitch transport automatically. No configuration changes; the
`running` field keeps its existing meaning.

## Evidence

Extends the existing Twitch test suite (all extension tests pass, 185/185):

- `extensions/twitch/src/twitch-client.test.ts` — a post-handshake
  `onDisconnect` now notifies subscribers with `connected: false` and the
  disconnect reason; the registration cleanly unsubscribes.
- `extensions/twitch/src/plugin.lifecycle.test.ts` — driving the real
  `gateway.startAccount` path, a monitor-reported transport drop emits
  `connected: false` while `running` is never cleared (asserted explicitly).

These exercise the real `TwitchClientManager` / `monitorTwitchProvider` /
`gateway.startAccount` / `buildChannelSummary` code paths with only the external
`@twurple/chat` chat client stubbed — the same proof approach accepted for the
qqbot transport-status fix in #100127.

target.title: fix(pairing): advertise reachable Tailnet routes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mobile pairing setup codes advertised one bind-derived LAN address. A phone connected through Tailscale could scan a valid code but fail because that LAN address was unreachable from its current network.

Fixes #100280.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep the existing `url` field for old clients and add a bounded, ordered `urls` list.
- Discover only persistent, node-local, tailnet-only HTTPS Tailscale Serve roots that proxy the active Gateway port. Exclude public Funnel and load-balanced Service routes.
- Propagate candidates through the Gateway protocol, CLI, device-pair plugin, and Control UI.
- Let iOS probe candidates before persisting credentials, select the first reachable endpoint, and invalidate stale/reentrant setup attempts.

## User Impact

LAN setup remains unchanged. When a matching Tailscale Serve route exists, new iOS clients can use the same setup code on either the local network or Tailnet and automatically save the reachable route. Older and non-iOS clients continue using the original primary URL.

target.title: fix(discord): limit implicit reply references to first chunk
target.body:
﻿Closes #99068

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users with `replyToMode: "first"` could receive one native reply notification per physical chunk when a single long agent reply was split into multiple Discord messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord now carries a source-aware first-chunk-only flag from outbound delivery into the shared send layer. The flag is only enabled for implicit single-use reply targets, so explicit `[[reply_to_*]]` replies and all-mode replies keep their existing reusable native reply behavior while the implicit turn reply no longer fans out across every physical text or media-caption chunk.

The payload send path now uses the same reply fanout contract for each physical Discord send, including `audioAsVoice`, native Discord payload media, component follow-up media, and classic component media downgrades. That closes the reviewer-noted gap where one captured implicit reply id could be reused across voice/text/media/component sends.

The related open PR #99083 is not a strong blocker for this replacement shape: it now has proof, but its mode-only suppression was previously flagged for collapsing explicit first-mode chunk replies. This PR uses the reply source to avoid that compatibility regression while keeping all-mode and explicit reply tags reusable.

## User Impact

Long Discord replies in first/batched implicit reply modes now quote the source message only on the first physical Discord message, avoiding repeated reply notifications for one logical answer. Explicit reply tags and all-mode replies remain reusable across chunks and payload sends as before.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(ios): restore in-flight runs after reconnect
target.body:
Part of #100197. Supersedes the stacked `afterSeq` design in #100267.

## What Problem This Solves

When iOS backgrounds, reconnects, changes sessions, or misses an event sequence, it can lose ownership of a run that is still active on the Gateway. The transcript may look idle, Abort disappears, and a second send becomes possible while the first run is still working.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already exposes the canonical active-run snapshot through `chat.history.inFlightRun`; the TUI already consumes that contract. This rewrite removes every proposed `afterSeq` protocol/client change and restores ownership from the existing snapshot instead.

The shared Apple chat model now:

- adopts active run ID and buffered text during bootstrap, foreground resume, sequence-gap recovery, immediate post-send refresh, delayed retries, and completion refreshes;
- orders history snapshots against newer live deltas, terminal events, session messages, session switches, agent changes, and concurrent history requests;
- keeps ownership stable when another client streams a different run in the same session;
- scopes bare-global/default-agent aliases and non-default agent-qualified global sessions without cross-agent transcript adoption;
- distinguishes current Gateway negative state via `sessionInfo.hasActiveRun` from legacy gateways that omit active-run metadata;
- preserves live/provisional transcript rows when delayed history arrives, including identical replies from different turns;
- rearms timeouts safely and clears silent completed/failed runs from authoritative current-Gateway state.

Codex app-server source confirms a turn becomes `InProgress` with no message items before later `AgentMessageDelta` notifications (`codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359`). That is why an active run with an empty buffered string is still valid ownership.

## User Impact

Returning to iOS or macOS chat no longer loses an active response. Streaming text, tool state, Abort, and the send lock recover without adding a Gateway protocol or cursor, while older Gateways retain the prior transcript-based completion fallback.

## Evidence

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatViewModelTests` — 129/129 passed after rebase, including unrelated session activity without a chat-run snapshot.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos` — passed after rebase.
- SwiftFormat lint with `config/swiftformat` — clean for every touched Swift file.
- Final full-branch Codex autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings after separating session-wide activity from chat-run ownership.
- Direct Gateway contract review: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`, `src/gateway/server-session-events.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/session-active-runs.ts`.
- Direct Codex contract review at `be33f80bc65159c094ecd06bf155afa3061ce23d`: `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs:155-183`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs:359-367`, and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs:375-378`.

Visual reconnect/background proof is requested separately on this exact head.
